sections.h2: Where is Normal and how did it get its name?
sections.html:
Normal is a town in McLean County, central Illinois, and it forms the Bloomington-Normal pair with its neighbor Bloomington. Its land area is about 18.3 square miles. The 2020 census counted 52,736 people, and the Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate is 53,275.

The town was laid out on June 7, 1854 as North Bloomington. In 1865 it took the name Normal after Illinois State Normal University, the teacher-training school now called Illinois State University, and it was incorporated on February 25, 1867. Normal is the seventh largest Illinois community outside the Chicago metropolitan area.

Uptown Normal, built around a roundabout, holds the town hall, the Amtrak station, the Children's Discovery Museum, hotels and the restored Normal Theater. The original town was laid out mostly south of the rail lines, and the major retail center is on Veterans Parkway on the east side.

sections.h2: How much does Illinois State University shape the Normal housing market?
sections.html:
It is a major driver. Illinois State University, founded in 1857 as the first public university in the state, has a 350-acre campus in town, and Heartland Community College, founded in 1990, adds more students. The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 figures show the effect:

MeasureNormal
Owner-occupied housing unit rate54.8%
Median value of owner-occupied homes$213,600
Median gross rent$965
Households20,387
Persons per household2.27
Lived in the same house a year earlier75.5%
Mean travel time to work16.5 minutes
Median household income$64,785

Only about 55% of housing units are owner-occupied, and a quarter of residents moved within the past year. Rentals are a normal part of the market here, and Normal's rules for rental licenses and short-term stays come up in many sales.

sections.h2: Does Normal require a license for rental property?
sections.html:
Yes, for multi-family rentals. Section 11.8-1 of the Town code, as posted by the Town, says no one may operate an apartment, rooming house, multiple-use dwelling, hotel, motel, bed and breakfast or duplex (except the owner-occupied side) without a rental occupancy license issued by the Building Commissioner.

  • Licenses run January 1 through December 31 of a year.
  • A license belongs to one owner and one property and cannot be transferred without a transfer fee and a completed application from the new owner.
  • The code lists a change of owner as one reason a license may be revoked.
  • An inspection takes place before any license is issued, and the owner must give the Town access to the units. A tenant or owner who refuses can face a search warrant request.
  • Appeals of a refusal or revocation go to the Building Commissioner within 30 days.
  • Penalties run from $25 to $200 for a first offense and $50 to $500 for later ones, with each day counted as a separate offense.

An owner selling a duplex or small apartment building should tell the buyer that the license does not move with the deed. The Inspections Department is at 1 Uptown Circle, phone 309-454-9581.

sections.h2: What are Normal's short-term rental rules for a seller or buyer?
sections.html:
Short-term rentals in Normal need a Town business license. On June 16, 2025 the Town Council passed Ordinance 6028 on short-term rental licensing. The Town's business license page also says STRs are prohibited in R-1 and R-2 zoning unless the property is the owner-occupant's primary residence.

  • In R-1 zoning, no more than 2 unrelated people, or 1 family plus 1 unrelated person, may stay.
  • In R-2 and R-3 zoning, the limit is 4 unrelated people.
  • Parking is allowed only on hard surfaces, and street parking is capped at 24 hours unless a sign says otherwise.
  • Parties, meetings and other events are not allowed.
  • The Short-Term Rental Tax form and payment are due by the 25th of the month after collection.

The business license itself carries no fee, but the Town issues it only after taxes and debts owed to the Town are paid. If you are selling a house that has been used as an STR, ask the Town how the license and any tax account will be handled so the buyer does not inherit a balance.

sections.h2: How are deeds recorded in McLean County?
sections.html:
The McLean County Clerk's Recording Division records them, at 115 E. Washington Street, Room M104, in Bloomington. The phone is 309-888-5170 and the office is open Monday through Friday, 8 am to 4:30 pm. Voters moved the old Recorder's duties into the County Clerk's office by referendum on November 6, 2012, effective December 31, 2013.

The county lists what every deed must include:

  • A statement of exemption or a transfer tax declaration.
  • The name of the person who prepared it.
  • Where future tax statements are to be sent.
  • A notary seal, date and signature, with original signatures; photocopies and digital signatures are not accepted.
  • A complete legal description with the permanent index number.
  • A complete return address.

The recorder's staff cannot give legal advice or legal descriptions, so have the deed prepared by an attorney or title company.

sections.h2: What does the Rivian plant mean for homes in Normal?
sections.html:
It has changed the local job picture. Diamond-Star Motors, a Mitsubishi and Chrysler venture, opened a manufacturing plant in Normal in 1986. Mitsubishi closed it on May 31, 2016, and Rivian bought it in January 2017. Rivian has built all-electric vehicles there since 2021, and the plant is the company's largest in the United States.

Interstates 55, 74 and 39 serve the town, and I-39 ends at Normal. U.S. 51, U.S. 150, Illinois Route 9 and historic Route 66 pass through. The Amtrak station at 11 Uptown Circle has four Lincoln Service trains a day in each direction between Chicago and St. Louis, and Connect Transit runs 16 fixed routes. Central Illinois Regional Airport is just over the line in Bloomington, about five miles from Uptown.

The town sits inside McLean County Unit District No. 5, which runs Normal Community High School, Normal Community West High School and Kingsley Junior High School. Illinois State University operates two schools of its own, University High School and Thomas Metcalf Elementary. Private options include Epiphany Catholic School, Calvary Christian Academy, Cornerstone Christian Academy and Bloom Community School.

Census data show that 97.6% of adults age 25 and older have a high school diploma and 52.9% hold a bachelor's degree or higher. The average trip to work takes 16.5 minutes.

sections.h2: How does Normal weather affect an older house?
sections.html:
The 1991 to 2020 NOAA normals show about 39.4 inches of precipitation a year, 20.1 inches of snow and 113 days with measurable precipitation. Summer highs average 86 degrees Fahrenheit in July, while January lows average about 16. The record high is 114 and the record low is minus 24.

That range is hard on roofs, gutters, window seals and furnaces. If your house is older, a recent roof receipt or a furnace service record answers some of the first questions a buyer's inspector will ask.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Normal rental property to another landlord?
faqs.a: Yes. The rental occupancy license is specific to one owner and one property, so the buyer applies in their own name, pays a transfer fee and passes an inspection. Ask the Inspections Department at 309-454-9581 how that will be handled before closing.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for a Normal house?
faqs.a: At the McLean County Clerk's Recording Division, 115 E. Washington Street, Room M104, Bloomington, phone 309-888-5170. The deed needs a transfer tax declaration or exemption statement, original notarized signatures and a full legal description with the permanent index number.

faqs.q: Are short-term rentals allowed in Normal?
faqs.a: They are allowed with a Town business license, but not in R-1 or R-2 zoning unless the property is the owner's primary residence. The Town adopted Ordinance 6028 on June 16, 2025, and guest limits depend on the zoning district.

faqs.q: What do Census figures say about home values in Normal?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau's median value of an owner-occupied home is $213,600 for 2020 to 2024. The town has a 54.8% owner-occupied rate, a $965 median gross rent and a median household income of $64,785.

faqs.q: How long is the commute from Normal to work?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau puts the mean travel time to work at 16.5 minutes for 2020 to 2024. Interstates 55, 74 and 39 serve the town, and Connect Transit runs 16 fixed routes.
